title: Readiness gates: GPU health + networking/DNS/TLS + runtime smoke test (pass/fail + operator errors)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Goal
Implement automated readiness gates that run after bootstrap but before control plane marks capacity Ready. Gates must validate:
1) GPU health
2) Networking (incl DNS + TLS)
3) Runtime smoke test

These checks should be:
- Deterministic and low-flake (avoid heavy perf benchmarking; perf-canary is ENG-2747)
- Fast (target < 12 minutes for full gate suite on a new pool)
- Produce actionable, operator-facing errors with remediation hints + runbook links
- Emit structured stage results + metrics (pass/fail + duration + categorized failure reason)

Context
We’ve had multiple pilots where infra is provisioned but the pool is not actually usable: bad driver/firmware combos, DNS/TLS problems reaching registries/control plane, and runtime bootstraps that "look green" but fail on first request. This ticket defines the minimal set of readiness gates to prevent routing from advertising broken capacity.

Scope
- A readiness-gates runner invoked by provisioner during the "Validating" stage
- Pass/fail criteria for each check
- Error model: stable error codes + human-readable message + suggested next action
- Output artifact: a single JSON summary per run (also logged as structured event)

Non-goals
- Full performance validation (handled in ENG-2747)
- Hardware procurement/quota validation beyond basic "GPU visible" checks

Where it runs
- Default: in-cluster (Kubernetes Job) with read-only cluster permissions + limited node access where required
- GPU checks require node-level inspection; approach:
  - Use a privileged daemonset/job in a dedicated namespace (redwood-provisioning) deployed only during validation, then removed
  - Minimal privileges: access to /dev/nvidia*, read nvidia-smi, optional DCGM if present on golden image

Readiness gate suite

A) GPU Health Check (Gate: gpu_health)

Inputs
- Expected GPU count per node (from pool config / IaC outputs)
- Expected driver major/minor range (from golden image manifest)
- Region/SKU (for diagnostics allowlist; avoid SKU-specific hardcoding)

Checks (per node)
1. GPU enumeration
   - Command: nvidia-smi -L
   - Pass: detects >= expected_gpus_per_node and UUIDs stable across two reads (5s apart)
   - Fail code: GPU_ENUM_MISMATCH

2. Driver presence + version
   - Command: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader
   - Pass: all nodes report a driver_version within the allowed range for the image/runtime compatibility matrix
   - Fail code: GPU_DRIVER_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED

3. Health indicators (ECC + retired pages)
   - Commands:
     - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile,total --format=csv,noheader
     - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=retired_pages.single_bit_retirement,retired_pages.double_bit_retirement --format=csv,noheader
   - Pass:
     - Uncorrected ECC volatile == 0
     - Double-bit retired pages == 0
     - Single-bit retired pages <= 1 (tolerate 1 w/ warning; fail if >1)
   - Fail code: GPU_ECC_OR_RETIRED_PAGES

4. Recent Xid / kernel errors
   - Command: journalctl -k --since "-30 min" | grep -E "NVRM: Xid" (best effort)
   - Pass: no Xid entries in last 30 minutes
   - Fail code: GPU_XID_DETECTED

5. Optional: DCGM quick diag (if dcgmi present)
   - Command: dcgmi diag -r 1 (or equivalent "short" suite)
   - Pass: overall "Pass"; allow known benign warnings to be logged but not fail
   - Fail code: GPU_DCGM_DIAG_FAILED

GPU gate pass/fail criteria
- Fail the overall gate if ANY node fails checks 1–4 (or 5 if DCGM is present and explicitly enabled)
- If only "single-bit retired pages == 1" occurs, mark as PASS_WITH_WARNINGS and include node list in summary; do not block Ready but raise a non-paging alert (see Observability notes)

Operator-facing error message template (GPU)
- Title: "GPU health check failed on <pool_id>"
- Body fields:
  - failing_nodes: <comma-separated>
  - first_error_code: <code>
  - excerpt: <relevant command output lines>
  - next_steps:
    - If ECC/Xid: "cordon & replace node(s)" (link to runbook section)
    - If driver mismatch: "verify golden image version / node image promotion" (link)

B) Networking / DNS / TLS Check (Gate: network_connectivity)

Checks
1. DNS resolution
   - Targets:
     - control plane API hostname (region-specific)
     - artifact registry hostname (container registry)
     - telemetry endpoint hostname (metrics/logs)
   - Commands:
     - nslookup <host> OR dig +time=2 +tries=1 <host>
   - Pass: resolves within 2s for all targets from within cluster network namespace
   - Fail code: NET_DNS_RESOLUTION_FAILED

2. TLS handshake
   - Targets: same hostnames + any internal mTLS endpoints used by bootstrap
   - Command: openssl s_client -connect <host:443> -servername <host> -brief (timeout 5s)
   - Pass:
     - handshake succeeds
     - certificate verifies (system trust store)
     - time drift check: validate node time within 60s of NTP (see #4)
   - Fail code: NET_TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED

3. Outbound egress reachability
   - Minimal HTTP GET:
     - curl -fsS https://<control-plane>/healthz
     - curl -fsS https://<registry>/v2/ (expect 401/403 acceptable; network success)
   - Pass: request completes and returns any HTTP response (including auth errors)
   - Fail code: NET_EGRESS_UNREACHABLE

4. Time sync / skew
   - Command: timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized -p TimeUSec; optionally compare to a trusted time endpoint
   - Pass: NTPSynchronized=yes OR time skew < 60s
   - Fail code: NET_TIME_SKEW

5. MTU sanity (best effort)
   - Command: ip link show; ping -M do -s <size> to a known internal endpoint (if allowed)
   - Pass: no obvious MTU mismatch causing fragmentation for typical payloads (we log only; do not hard fail unless we see repeated failures in pilots)
   - Result: warning only for now

Network gate pass/fail criteria
- Fail if any of checks 1–4 fails from the cluster context
- Log MTU check as warning-only unless we have a crisp, low-flake test

Operator-facing error message template (Network)
- Title: "Networking readiness failed (<code>)"
- Body fields:
  - failing_check: dns|tls|egress|time
  - target: <hostname>
  - resolver: <cluster DNS IP> (if available)
  - excerpt: <first 20 lines>
  - next_steps: "Check VPC route tables / SG egress / cluster DNS" (link to dedicated-pool provisioning runbook)

C) Runtime Smoke Test (Gate: runtime_smoke)

Intent
Confirm the runtime is installed, can start, can load a minimal model, and can serve a trivial request. This is NOT a perf benchmark; it should be stable across SKUs.

Preconditions
- Helm chart pinned and deployed by bootstrap stage
- Control plane registration should exist but pool must not be advertised to routing until all gates pass

Checks
1. Runtime pods ready
   - kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod -l app=redwood-runtime -n <pool-ns> --timeout=10m
   - Pass: all expected pods ready (based on config replica count)
   - Fail code: RUNTIME_PODS_NOT_READY

2. Health endpoint
   - curl -fsS http://<runtime-service>/health
   - Pass: 200 OK and body contains "ok" (or agreed stable response)
   - Fail code: RUNTIME_HEALTHCHECK_FAILED

3. Minimal inference request
   - Request: generate 8 tokens from a static prompt using the "smoke" model (small, cached in registry; e.g., a tiny Llama variant or a dedicated smoke artifact)
   - Pass:
     - returns success status
     - output tokens count >= 1
     - completes within 60s end-to-end
   - Fail code: RUNTIME_INFERENCE_FAILED

4. GPU utilization observed (sanity)
   - Optional: sample nvidia-smi during inference; ensure non-zero utilization at least once (best effort)
   - Warning-only (avoid flakes)

Runtime gate pass/fail criteria
- Fail if checks 1–3 fail
- Log check 4 as warning-only

Output + integration
- Emit a single JSON summary to logs and as a structured provisioning event:
  - gates: gpu_health, network_connectivity, runtime_smoke
  - for each gate: status PASS|FAIL|PASS_WITH_WARNINGS, duration_ms, error_code (if any), error_message (short), remediation_hint (short)
  - node_failures list (stringified)
- Provisioner behavior:
  - Any FAIL => provisioning run transitions to Failed (or stays in Validating with retry policy; see ENG-48241/ENG-2742 semantics)
  - PASS_WITH_WARNINGS => continue to Ready, but emit warning event + create ticket if configured

Error codes (initial set)
GPU
- GPU_ENUM_MISMATCH
- GPU_DRIVER_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED
- GPU_ECC_OR_RETIRED_PAGES
- GPU_XID_DETECTED
- GPU_DCGM_DIAG_FAILED

Network
- NET_DNS_RESOLUTION_FAILED
- NET_TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED
- NET_EGRESS_UNREACHABLE
- NET_TIME_SKEW

Runtime
- RUNTIME_PODS_NOT_READY
- RUNTIME_HEALTHCHECK_FAILED
- RUNTIME_INFERENCE_FAILED

Metrics (emitted by ENG-2748 plumbing; this ticket defines names/labels)
- provisioner.readiness_gate.duration_ms (histogram)
  - labels: gate_name, region, sku_family
- provisioner.readiness_gate.result (counter)
  - labels: gate_name, result, error_code

Acceptance criteria
- Can run gates on a staging pool and reliably get PASS on healthy pools
- On induced failure (e.g., break DNS, force bad driver version, kill runtime pods), gate fails with correct error_code and actionable error_message
- Total time for gates <= 12 minutes for typical pool
- All failures are correlated to provisioning run ID / pool ID and visible in logs

Implementation notes
- Prefer Go-based gate runner library used by provisioner service, with a small container image for in-cluster job execution.
- Avoid fragile parsing: where possible use CSV queries from nvidia-smi.
- Timeouts must be explicit and short per check; no indefinite waits.

Runbook links
- Confluence: Dedicated pool provisioning runbook ("Validation failures" section)
- Confluence: Image build and rollout runbook ("Driver mismatch" section)

Open questions
- Do we want to hard-fail on DCGM diag by default or feature-flag it per SKU? (proposal: off by default, on for H100/A100 once stable)
- Do we require runtime smoke model to be pre-pulled during imaging to reduce registry dependencies? (proposal: yes for staging pilot; optional for prod)
comments: 2024-02-22 (Vanessa Ortiz): Creating this as P0. We keep getting handoffs where infra is “up” but unusable. Need crisp gates + error codes so oncall isn’t guessing.
2024-02-26 (Rafael Mendes): Drafted initial gate list and error codes. Strong preference to keep DCGM optional until we’ve validated it across regions/SKUs (we’ve seen flakes on A10 in the past).
2024-02-27 (Victor Alvarez): Added DNS/TLS targets we should test from inside cluster. Suggest allowing 401/403 from registry as success (network is fine; auth can be separate).
2024-03-01 (Gabe Wilson): Implemented prototype runner as a k8s Job; GPU checks need privileged mode. Will scope privileges to namespace redwood-provisioning and delete job/DS after run.

2024-03-04 (Miles Thornton): Please ensure all checks have hard timeouts; we can’t have validation hang for 45 minutes and block the entire run. Also label metrics by sku_family not raw sku to avoid high cardinality.
2024-03-06 (Aisha Bello): Confirmed metric names align with time-to-ready dashboards work. PASS_WITH_WARNINGS should still emit a counter so we can track frequency.

2024-03-08 (Rafael Mendes): Staging pilot: induced DNS failure -> NET_DNS_RESOLUTION_FAILED surfaced correctly w/ resolver IP in message. Runtime smoke failure case (pods not ready) also produces correct error_code. Total validation time ~9m on staging pool.
2024-03-12 (Harish Reddy): Operator feedback: error messages are much better; request to include “what command was run” in the failure summary (at least for GPU and TLS) for faster triage.
2024-03-15 (Rafael Mendes): Marking Done. Follow-up: integrate perf-canary thresholds (ENG-2747) and decide on DCGM default for H100 pools after we collect more data.
